paper_title: Improved axion emissivity from a supernova via nucleon-nucleon bremsstrahlung
notes: New SN 1987A energy-loss bound derived from an improved N-N bremsstrahlung axion emissivity (over an order of magnitude reduction vs naive OPE). The paper's Lagrangian Eq.(2.2), L=(g_ai/2m_N) N-bar gamma_mu gamma_5 N d^mu a, is already the canonical 2m_N convention, so g_ap is directly canonical (no conversion). Headline coupling result is for the KSVZ hadronic axion model (C_an=0, C_ap=-0.47), so the bound is on the axion-PROTON coupling. Realistic SN model at t_pb=1s (Table 2, OPE+corr.+MS, the paper's full/best calculation): g_ap = 12e-10 = 1.2e-9 (m_a <~ 15 meV, f_a >~ 4.0e8 GeV). Consistent with the general bound Eq.(3.3): g_an^2 + 0.61 g_ap^2 + 0.53 g_an g_ap <~ 8.26e-19, which with g_an=0 gives g_ap <~ sqrt(8.26e-19/0.61)=1.16e-9. Per the task card's combination rule, I report the single canonical coupling g_ap with g_an set to 0 (this is exactly the KSVZ case since C_an=0). This is a mass-independent energy-loss coupling bound (valid for m_a << T~30 MeV, free-streaming regime g_aN<~1e-6); reported as a flat horizontal line. The mass range 1e-3 to 1 eV is representative of the SN-relevant window the paper discusses (meV-eV); the bound value is the robust quantity, the range endpoints are approximate. Bound is an order-of-magnitude energy-loss criterion (L_a <~ L_nu ~ 2e52 erg/s), not a formal statistical CL, hence confidence_level=null. The paper also quotes a weaker schematic-model value (Table 1: g_ap=9e-10) and, for comparison, a neutron-coupling bound g_an<2.8e-10 from another work [67] (not the paper's own result). Analogous own bound on g_an alone (g_ap=0) would be sqrt(8.26e-19)=9.1e-10.
